citeAs: Paperno, Denis, Germán Kruszewski, Angeliki Lazaridou, Quan Ngoc Pham, Raffaella Bernardi, Sandro Pezzelle, Marco Baroni, Gemma Boleda, and Raquel Fernández. (2016). The LAMBADA dataset: Word prediction requiring a broad discourse context. Proceedings of the 54th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics.
creator: Denis Paperno, Germán Kruszewski, Angeliki Lazaridou, Quan Ngoc Pham, Raffaella Bernardi, Sandro Pezzelle, Marco Baroni, Gemma Boleda, Raquel Fernández (CIMeC - Center for Mind/Brain Sciences, University of Trento; Institute for Logic, Language & Computation, University of Amsterdam)
description: LAMBADA is a dataset for evaluating text understanding with a word prediction task. It consists of narrative passages from the Book Corpus where human subjects can guess the last word of the target sentence when given the full passage, but not when given only the target sentence, requiring broad discourse context.
name: LAMBADA
publisher: CIMeC - Center for Mind/Brain Sciences, University of Trento
rai:annotationsPerItem: At least 2 successful broad-context guesses and up to 10 unsuccessful sentence-only judgments per item; in step 3, subjects were allowed 3 guesses per sentence.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper reports filtering outcomes and validation criteria for human judgments: 84–86% of items were discarded at step 1, an additional 6–7% at step 2, and another 3–5% at step 3. Passages were included only if two consecutive subjects exactly matched the target word from the whole passage and no subject out of ten could provide it from local context only, even with 3 guesses.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: A three-step crowdsourcing protocol was used. First, one human subject guessed the target word from the whole passage; if correct, a second subject guessed from the whole passage; if also correct, more subjects guessed from the target sentence only until the word was guessed or 10 unsuccessful guesses were reached. Items were kept only if two whole-passage subjects guessed correctly and no sentence-only subject guessed the word. The same subject was not allowed to judge the same item in both passage and sentence conditions.
rai:dataBiases: The paper explicitly notes a strong bias toward target words whose lemma appears in the context and an overrepresentation of proper nouns: more than 80% of LAMBADA passages include the target word in the context, and 48% of target words are proper nouns. The authors also chose unpublished novels to minimize the usefulness of general world knowledge and external resources.
rai:dataCollection: The dataset was built from the Book Corpus. Passages were constructed from unpublished novels, with a context of the minimum number of complete sentences before the target sentence needed to cumulatively contain at least 50 tokens. The authors randomly divided novels into training and development+testing partitions, then built LAMBADA from the latter and further split it into development and test by novel. Passages were first filtered with language models, then evaluated by human subjects to retain only examples guessable from broad context but not from the target sentence alone.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw source data were unpublished novels from the Book Corpus. After duplicate removal and filtering of potentially offensive material with a stop word list, the corpus contained 5,325 novels and 465 million words.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataLimitations: The paper notes that the inclusion criteria are very strict, using an exact-match hit-or-miss approach that excludes passages where plausible or synonymous continuations might fit. Cost considerations prevented using more subjects at stage 1, which could have improved filtering quality. The dataset is also biased toward proper nouns and cases where the target word occurs in the context.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The authors filtered out passages that were relatively easy for standard language models by excluding any passage whose target word had probability ≥0.00175 according to any of four language models. They also partitioned novels into disjoint training and development/test sets and further split development and test by novel to keep passages self-contained.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The source Book Corpus underwent duplicate removal and filtering of potentially offensive material with a stop word list. For LAMBADA construction, passages were defined using a minimum preceding context containing at least 50 tokens, and novels were split into disjoint partitions for training and development/testing.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended as a challenging benchmark to evaluate and encourage development of language models that can use broad discourse context for word prediction and natural language understanding.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: A combination of four language models was used to automatically filter candidate passages before human evaluation: a pre-trained recurrent neural network (RNN), a standard 4-gram model, an RNN trained on the Book Corpus, and a feed-forward model.
